70d5616c-3a0e-4600-9e6d-f927fcde43a5.name: Advanced Diploma in Philosophy
70d5616c-3a0e-4600-9e6d-f927fcde43a5.description: The Advanced Diploma in Philosophy builds on the Diploma in Theology with a specialised focus on philosophy, developing foundational skills for critical study of Christian texts alongside philosophical analysis and argument. Students engage theological, scriptural and philosophical knowledge and apply it to their own and other contexts, including through practical ministry settings. It is delivered by two University of Divinity member colleges (Catholic Theological College and Yarra Theological Union) and can be undertaken on its own or combined with the Bachelor of Theology as a dual qualification.
70d5616c-3a0e-4600-9e6d-f927fcde43a5.curriculum: The award consists of 288 points across 16 standard undergraduate units: 18 points each in Old Testament, New Testament, Church History and Systematic Theology, 144 points in Philosophy, 36 further points from Biblical Studies and/or Christian Thought and History, and 36 further points in any discipline. Standard full-time duration is 2 years (up to 8 years part-time).
70d5616c-3a0e-4600-9e6d-f927fcde43a5.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is one of an Australian Year 12 qualification or the Diploma in Theology; probationary admission is not available. Up to 180 points of credit may be granted, including 144 points toward the Diploma of Catholic Youth Ministry (10603NAT or 11013NAT) split across Biblical Studies, Systematic Theology and Mission and Ministry, per the University's Credit Policy.
70d5616c-3a0e-4600-9e6d-f927fcde43a5.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium secondary or tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

9f38bb7d-b0ee-40d2-b040-035fdba35bf6.name: Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry
9f38bb7d-b0ee-40d2-b040-035fdba35bf6.description: The Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry builds on the Diploma in Theology, deepening students' understanding of Biblical Studies and Christian Thought and History alongside further study in practical ministry. Graduates gain skills to articulate theological and scriptural knowledge and apply it to ministry practice and culturally relevant contexts. It is delivered across 12 University of Divinity member colleges nationally and can be combined with the Bachelor of Ministry or Bachelor of Theology as a dual qualification.
9f38bb7d-b0ee-40d2-b040-035fdba35bf6.curriculum: The award consists of 288 points across 16 standard undergraduate units: 18 points each in Old Testament, New Testament, Church History and Systematic Theology, 36 points in Practical Theology, 36 further points from Biblical Studies and/or Christian Thought and History, and 144 further points in any discipline. Standard full-time duration is 2 years (up to 8 years part-time).
9f38bb7d-b0ee-40d2-b040-035fdba35bf6.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is one of an Australian Year 12 qualification, the Diploma in Ministry or the Diploma in Theology; probationary admission is not available. Up to 180 points of credit may be granted, including for the Diploma in Ageing and Pastoral or Spiritual Care and the Diploma of Catholic Youth Ministry, per the University's Credit Policy.
9f38bb7d-b0ee-40d2-b040-035fdba35bf6.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium secondary or tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

dedccf7a-7c93-4122-93fd-7f264b4b8e48.name: Bachelor of Counselling
dedccf7a-7c93-4122-93fd-7f264b4b8e48.description: The Bachelor of Counselling trains students to become both competent and wise counselling practitioners, grounded in virtues such as hope, courage and compassion, for work with young people, couples, families and diverse communities. Alongside clinical and ethical practice, students learn about the use of AI in mental health and basic business skills to prepare them for the profession. The course is delivered through Australian Lutheran College and is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association. This course is currently available to domestic students only.
dedccf7a-7c93-4122-93fd-7f264b4b8e48.curriculum: The award consists of 432 points (24 units) over 3 years. Year 1 (144 points) covers core units including Expressing Integrity Through Excellence in Academic and Professional Communication, Self, Profession and Society, Introduction to Counselling, Engaging Diversity, Introduction to Psychology and Data Literacy for Clinicians. Year 2 (144 points) covers Human Development Personality and Identity, Working with Children Adolescents and Older Adults, Trauma-Informed Counselling, Counselling Ethics the Law and Best-Practice, and Self-Care and the Workplace (with 36 hours on-job training), plus 36 points of electives. Year 3 (144 points) covers Complex Clients (Neurodiversity, Addictions and Personality Disorders), Virtues-Based Counselling, Emerging Technologies AI and the Business of Counselling, a Capstone Project, 36 points of supervised placement (150 hours including 20 hours counselling and 20 hours supervision) and 36 points of electives. Students may exit after Year 1 with the Diploma in Counselling or after Year 2 with the Advanced Diploma in Counselling.
dedccf7a-7c93-4122-93fd-7f264b4b8e48.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is an Australian secondary school qualification or equivalent; probationary admission is available into the first (Diploma-level) year. Applicants must have regular access to a computer supporting video and standard software, and by the end of their eighth first-year unit must provide a national police check and a Working with Children check (both at the candidate's expense), with COVID-19 vaccination evidence potentially required for clinical placement depending on state legislation.
dedccf7a-7c93-4122-93fd-7f264b4b8e48.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy, the standard institutional threshold that would apply were the course to open to overseas students; the course's own live page currently lists it as available to domestic students only, with no CRICOS registration.

1ade0e99-3b37-4642-9c54-9eaf88a6191e.name: Bachelor of Ministry
1ade0e99-3b37-4642-9c54-9eaf88a6191e.description: The Bachelor of Ministry prepares students for the practice of ministry, establishing foundations through the study of scriptures, theological traditions and historical and contemporary contexts, with concentrated study in ministry praxis. Graduates gain a coherent vision of ministry and the ability to apply theological reflection to shape their practice. It is delivered across 9 University of Divinity member colleges and can be combined with the Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry or the Bachelor of Theology as a dual qualification; it also offers a specific pathway into the Master of Social Work at Flinders University.
1ade0e99-3b37-4642-9c54-9eaf88a6191e.curriculum: The award consists of 432 points across 24 standard undergraduate units: 72 points in Biblical Studies (at least 18 points in each Testament), 36 points in Church History, 72 points in Systematic Theology, 36 points in Practical Theology, 72 points in Pastoral Theology and Ministry Studies (including at least 36 points of Supervised Theological Field Education or Clinical Pastoral Education), an 18-point Capstone unit, and 126 further points in any discipline, with restrictions on Level 1 point load. The Social Work pathway into Flinders University's Master of Social Work requires specific units including Sociology for Mission and Ministry, Community Ministry, Justice and Community Development, Ministry in Liminal Spaces, Introduction to Psychology, Engaging Diversity and Ecotheology.
1ade0e99-3b37-4642-9c54-9eaf88a6191e.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is one of an Australian Year 12 qualification, the Diploma in Ministry, the Diploma in Theology or the Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry; probationary admission is not available. Up to 288 points of credit may be granted, including for a prior Associate Degree or Advanced Diploma, an Australian Bachelor's degree, a 3-year professional teaching or nursing diploma, or specific ageing/pastoral care and Catholic Youth Ministry diplomas, per the University's Credit Policy.
1ade0e99-3b37-4642-9c54-9eaf88a6191e.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium secondary or tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

002ad8c7-b789-4f44-b992-767fa7e8f87b.name: Bachelor of Theology
002ad8c7-b789-4f44-b992-767fa7e8f87b.description: The Bachelor of Theology critically examines life and faith through the study of scriptures, theological traditions and historical contexts, broadening self-understanding and facilitating cultural engagement. Students develop knowledge across broad areas of theology with depth in particular interests, alongside research and communication skills, preparing graduates for further theological study and, where relevant, ministry-setting placements. It is the most widely delivered undergraduate award in the consortium, offered by 12 University of Divinity member colleges, and can be combined with the Advanced Diploma in Philosophy, the Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry, or the Bachelor of Ministry as a dual qualification.
002ad8c7-b789-4f44-b992-767fa7e8f87b.curriculum: The award consists of 432 points across 24 standard undergraduate units: 72 points in Biblical Studies (at least 18 points in each Testament), 36 points in Church History, 72 points in Systematic Theology, 36 points in Practical Theology, an 18-point Capstone unit, and 198 further points in any discipline, with a maximum of 216 points at Level 1 and a minimum of 108 points at Level 3 (including at least 36 points at Level 3 in Biblical Studies or Systematic Theology).
002ad8c7-b789-4f44-b992-767fa7e8f87b.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is one of an Australian Year 12 qualification, the Diploma in Ministry, the Diploma in Theology or the Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry; probationary admission is not available. Up to 288 points of credit may be granted, including for a prior Associate Degree or Advanced Diploma, an Australian Bachelor's degree, a 3-year professional teaching or nursing diploma, or specific ageing/pastoral care and Catholic Youth Ministry diplomas, per the University's Credit Policy.
002ad8c7-b789-4f44-b992-767fa7e8f87b.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium secondary or tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

16ced941-3dbd-4a3a-ae81-954da78a1d8a.name: Diploma in Theology
16ced941-3dbd-4a3a-ae81-954da78a1d8a.description: The Diploma in Theology introduces students to the key theological disciplines of Biblical Studies and Christian Thought and History, extendable through electives in practical ministry studies. Graduates gain sound foundational skills for the critical study of Christian texts and the ability to apply theological and scriptural knowledge to their own and other contexts. It is the entry-level undergraduate award in the consortium, offered by 12 University of Divinity member colleges, and serves as a pathway into the Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry, Advanced Diploma in Philosophy, Bachelor of Ministry or Bachelor of Theology.
16ced941-3dbd-4a3a-ae81-954da78a1d8a.curriculum: The award consists of 144 points across 8 standard undergraduate units: 36 points in Biblical Studies, 36 points in Christian Thought and History, and 72 further points in any discipline. Standard full-time duration is 1 year (up to 4 years part-time).
16ced941-3dbd-4a3a-ae81-954da78a1d8a.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is an Australian Year 12 qualification or equivalent, and probationary admission is available. Up to 90 points of credit may be granted, including for the Diploma in Ageing and Pastoral or Spiritual Care (10642NAT) or the Diploma in Ageing and Pastoral Care (91561NSW), per the University's Credit Policy.
16ced941-3dbd-4a3a-ae81-954da78a1d8a.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy, which sets one flat threshold across Diploma through Masters coursework level. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium secondary or tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

e4b8ef2a-e59e-42a9-8800-8913371d9ea8.name: Doctor of Philosophy (Theology)
e4b8ef2a-e59e-42a9-8800-8913371d9ea8.description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) is a graduate research degree enabling candidates to make an original contribution to knowledge in divinity and its associated disciplines and to develop as independent researchers. Guided by a supervisory team, candidates submit a thesis of 80,000 to 100,000 words demonstrating a systematic and critical understanding of a complex field, with specialised research skills for the advancement of learning or professional practice. It is a Higher Degree by Research supervised across 12 University of Divinity member colleges, and applicants are admitted only through the School of Graduate Research Committee.
e4b8ef2a-e59e-42a9-8800-8913371d9ea8.curriculum: As a research higher degree the course has no taught unit schedule; candidature involves satisfactory completion of confirmation of candidature, preparation and submission of a thesis (or equivalent) for examination, completion of an oral examination, compliance with Human Research Ethics Committee requirements, an annual progress report, at least 8 hours of annual research seminar or conference attendance, and presentation of at least one seminar or conference paper of 20 or more minutes between confirmation and thesis submission. Standard full-time duration is 3 years (minimum 2 years, up to 8 years part-time).
e4b8ef2a-e59e-42a9-8800-8913371d9ea8.admission_requirements: Applicants must be admitted by the School of Graduate Research Committee, which weighs research potential, proposal feasibility, available supervision and referee reports alongside minimum eligibility. Requirements include completion of a Master's by research, Master's by coursework, Graduate Diploma or 4-year Honours undergraduate degree in divinity or an associated discipline with a 75% average; a thesis or equivalent of at least 12,000 words graded at or above 75%; a research proposal identifying a research question, methodology and statement of original contribution; and at least two consenting supervisors meeting the Higher Degree by Research Policy's requirements. Probationary admission is not available.
e4b8ef2a-e59e-42a9-8800-8913371d9ea8.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5 (or equivalent: TOEFL Internet-based 91 with minimums of 25 Writing/22 Listening/22 Reading/22 Speaking, TOEFL Academic 577 with a Test of Written English score of at least 5.0, PTE Academic 65 with no communicative skill below 58, or C1 Advanced 176 with no component below 169), per Table 2 (Higher Degrees by Research, AQF 9 to 10) of the University of Divinity Higher Degree by Research Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium undergraduate or postgraduate study as set out in the same policy.

4d51e0f3-e8a8-4f31-be51-5e3e66a7360d.name: Graduate Certificate in Theology
4d51e0f3-e8a8-4f31-be51-5e3e66a7360d.description: The Graduate Certificate in Theology qualifies students in theological study by developing or deepening knowledge and skills across theological disciplines, serving as a foundation for further study and a means of critically engaging Christian thought and traditions. Graduates can articulate insights for Christian life and social engagement. It is delivered by 11 University of Divinity member colleges and is a common entry point into the Graduate Diploma in Theology or Master of Theological Studies.
4d51e0f3-e8a8-4f31-be51-5e3e66a7360d.curriculum: The award consists of 72 points (3 standard postgraduate units), comprising postgraduate foundational units from at least three Fields. Standard full-time duration is 6 months (up to 2 years part-time).
4d51e0f3-e8a8-4f31-be51-5e3e66a7360d.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is an undergraduate degree or 5 years of relevant work experience; probationary admission is not available. Applicants holding a Bachelor of Theology or Bachelor of Ministry may receive exemption without credit for 72 points of postgraduate foundational units across three disciplines from at least two Fields, per the University's Credit Policy.
4d51e0f3-e8a8-4f31-be51-5e3e66a7360d.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

c0df0e13-e447-4e43-9809-7700252de87a.name: Graduate Diploma in Divinity
c0df0e13-e447-4e43-9809-7700252de87a.description: The Graduate Diploma in Divinity allows students to explore multiple areas of interest in divinity and its associated disciplines, or to engage with one or two areas in depth, serving as a foundation for further study of theology or philosophy. It is delivered by 12 University of Divinity member colleges and may also be used as an exit point for eligible students enrolled in a Master's degree who meet its admission requirements.
c0df0e13-e447-4e43-9809-7700252de87a.curriculum: The award consists of 144 points (6 standard postgraduate units), made up entirely of postgraduate units in any discipline. Standard full-time duration is 1 year (up to 3 years part-time). Graduates who include a 16,000-word Minor Thesis may be eligible for admission to a higher degree by research.
c0df0e13-e447-4e43-9809-7700252de87a.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is one of an undergraduate degree or a Graduate Certificate from the University of Divinity; probationary admission is not available. Up to 72 points of credit may be granted, though not for study completed at institutions other than the University of Divinity, per the University's Credit Policy.
c0df0e13-e447-4e43-9809-7700252de87a.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

2deb3f2e-cea0-4a36-8f6e-05871524bc3e.name: Graduate Diploma in Spiritual Direction
2deb3f2e-cea0-4a36-8f6e-05871524bc3e.description: The Graduate Diploma in Spiritual Direction provides formation for the ministry of spiritual direction, with students exploring the dynamics of Christian spirituality through reflection on personal experience integrated with the literature. Graduates are equipped for the ministry of spiritual direction within their particular tradition. It is delivered through four distinct named formation programs at four member colleges (WellSpring at Whitley College, Siloam at Yarra Theological Union, Dayspring at Uniting College for Leadership and Theology, and a fourth program at St Francis College), each with its own core unit sequence, rather than one shared curriculum.
2deb3f2e-cea0-4a36-8f6e-05871524bc3e.curriculum: The award consists of 144 points (6 standard postgraduate units), delivered through one of four college-specific programs, each with its own core units, for example DD8202W Art of Spiritual Companioning 1 and DD8203W Art of Spiritual Companioning 2 (WellSpring, Whitley College); DD8701Y Religious Experience and the Christian Spiritual Tradition and DD8705Y Spiritual Direction Practicum I (Siloam, Yarra Theological Union); DD8740Z Contemplative Stance and Soul Care and DD8741Z Spiritual Direction Praxis 1 (Dayspring, Uniting College for Leadership and Theology); and DD8411Z Contemplative Presence and DD8412Z Spiritual Direction Foundations (St Francis College). Standard full-time duration is 1 year (up to 4 years part-time).
2deb3f2e-cea0-4a36-8f6e-05871524bc3e.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is one of an undergraduate degree or a Graduate Certificate; probationary admission is not available. Up to 72 points of credit may be granted, per the University's Credit Policy.
2deb3f2e-cea0-4a36-8f6e-05871524bc3e.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

8ae9a728-4c0f-48ef-a596-28142f9513a7.name: Graduate Diploma in Spirituality
8ae9a728-4c0f-48ef-a596-28142f9513a7.description: The Graduate Diploma in Spirituality allows students to explore their own spiritual experience in light of theological scholarship in spirituality, providing a substantial foundation for further study. Graduates are able to articulate insights for Christian practice and identity. It is a distinct award from the Graduate Diploma in Spiritual Direction, focused on the academic study of spirituality itself rather than formation for the spiritual-direction ministry, and is delivered by three member colleges (Catholic Theological College, Pilgrim Theological College and Whitley College).
8ae9a728-4c0f-48ef-a596-28142f9513a7.curriculum: The award consists of 144 points (6 standard postgraduate units): 96 points of postgraduate units in the disciplines of Spirituality or Spiritual Direction, and 48 further points of postgraduate units in any discipline. Standard full-time duration is 1 year (up to 3 years part-time).
8ae9a728-4c0f-48ef-a596-28142f9513a7.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is one of an undergraduate degree or a Graduate Certificate; probationary admission is not available. Up to 72 points of credit may be granted, per the University's Credit Policy.
8ae9a728-4c0f-48ef-a596-28142f9513a7.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

7500fdea-dd0d-4ca1-8e5c-cdd7d68ad9e4.name: Graduate Diploma in Theology
7500fdea-dd0d-4ca1-8e5c-cdd7d68ad9e4.description: The Graduate Diploma in Theology allows students to explore areas of interest in theology, providing a substantial foundation for further study and a means of engaging Christian thought and traditions. Graduates are able to articulate insights for Christian practice and identity. It is a distinct, more advanced award from the Graduate Certificate in Theology, delivered by 11 University of Divinity member colleges, and is a common step toward a Master's award.
7500fdea-dd0d-4ca1-8e5c-cdd7d68ad9e4.curriculum: The award consists of 144 points (6 standard postgraduate units): 72 points of postgraduate foundational units from at least three Fields, and 72 further points of postgraduate units in any discipline. Standard full-time duration is 1 year (up to 3 years part-time). Graduates who include a 16,000-word Minor Thesis may be eligible for admission to a higher degree by research.
7500fdea-dd0d-4ca1-8e5c-cdd7d68ad9e4.admission_requirements: Admission requires having obtained, or being qualified to obtain, a Bachelor's degree from the University of Divinity or a recognised university or college, or having obtained a Graduate Certificate from the University of Divinity; probationary admission is not available. Up to 72 points of credit may be granted, including 48 points for the Certificate of Religious Education of the Catholic Diocese of Sale, with exemption without credit of 72 points available to holders of a Bachelor of Theology or Bachelor of Ministry, per the University's Credit Policy.
7500fdea-dd0d-4ca1-8e5c-cdd7d68ad9e4.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

b27f0eaf-81bb-42c6-bbc0-6d4f6e9443c3.name: Master of Divinity
b27f0eaf-81bb-42c6-bbc0-6d4f6e9443c3.description: The Master of Divinity is a primary theological degree for students who already hold a degree in another area, enabling them to apply an advanced body of knowledge in divinity and its associated disciplines in ministry contexts. Students broaden their knowledge and skills to prepare for professional practice and further learning, including biblical or associated languages study. It is delivered by 11 University of Divinity member colleges and is a recognised pathway into the Doctor of Philosophy or Doctor of Professional Practice.
b27f0eaf-81bb-42c6-bbc0-6d4f6e9443c3.curriculum: The award consists of 432 points (18 standard postgraduate units): 48 points at postgraduate level in biblical or associated languages; 120 to 144 points at postgraduate foundational level (48 points in Biblical Studies, 48 in Christian Thought and History, 24 in Practical Theology); 192 to 240 points at postgraduate elective level (including at least 24 points each in Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Practical Theology); and either a capstone unit of at least 24 points or RQ9748M Minor Thesis (48 points). Standard full-time duration is 3 years (up to 9 years part-time).
b27f0eaf-81bb-42c6-bbc0-6d4f6e9443c3.admission_requirements: Admission requires successful completion of an undergraduate degree. Up to 216 points of credit may be granted, per the University's Credit Policy.
b27f0eaf-81bb-42c6-bbc0-6d4f6e9443c3.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

7a265010-f3cc-4d3e-8569-19c942328084.name: Master of Philosophy
7a265010-f3cc-4d3e-8569-19c942328084.description: The Master of Philosophy (MPhil) is a graduate research degree enabling candidates to further develop skills in independent and sustained research, contributing to a field of knowledge in divinity or one of its associated disciplines. Candidates present research in a thesis of around 40,000 words, and the award serves as a pathway to admission into the Doctor of Philosophy. It is a Higher Degree by Research supervised across all 12 University of Divinity member colleges, and applicants are admitted only through the School of Graduate Research Committee.
7a265010-f3cc-4d3e-8569-19c942328084.curriculum: As a research higher degree the course has no taught unit schedule; candidature involves satisfactory completion of confirmation of candidature, preparation and submission of a thesis (or equivalent) for examination, completion of an oral examination, compliance with Human Research Ethics Committee requirements, an annual progress report, at least 8 hours of annual research seminar or conference attendance, and presentation of at least one seminar or conference paper of 20 or more minutes once candidature is confirmed. Standard full-time duration is 1.5 years (minimum 1 year, up to 4 years part-time).
7a265010-f3cc-4d3e-8569-19c942328084.admission_requirements: Applicants must be admitted by the School of Graduate Research Committee, which weighs research potential, proposal feasibility, available supervision and referee reports alongside minimum eligibility. Requirements include completion of a Master's by research, Master's by coursework, Graduate Diploma or 4-year Honours undergraduate degree in divinity or an associated discipline with a 75% average; a thesis or equivalent of at least 12,000 words graded at or above 70%; a research proposal identifying a research question, methodology and statement of contribution; and at least two consenting supervisors meeting the Higher Degree by Research Policy's requirements. Probationary admission is not available.
7a265010-f3cc-4d3e-8569-19c942328084.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5 (or equivalent: TOEFL Internet-based 91 with minimums of 25 Writing/22 Listening/22 Reading/22 Speaking, TOEFL Academic 577 with a Test of Written English score of at least 5.0, PTE Academic 65 with no communicative skill below 58, or C1 Advanced 176 with no component below 169), per Table 2 (Higher Degrees by Research, AQF 9 to 10) of the University of Divinity Higher Degree by Research Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium undergraduate or postgraduate study as set out in the same policy.

c9210db7-77a8-486e-bc52-e4428a6daa8d.name: Master of Spiritual Direction
c9210db7-77a8-486e-bc52-e4428a6daa8d.description: The Master of Spiritual Direction enables students to acquire advanced knowledge of the theological and scriptural foundations of spiritual direction in the Christian tradition and to apply this knowledge in professional practice, including critical reflection on guiding an individual's spiritual experience. It is delivered by two member colleges (Uniting College for Leadership and Theology and Whitley College).
c9210db7-77a8-486e-bc52-e4428a6daa8d.curriculum: The award consists of 288 points (12 standard postgraduate units): 96 points of postgraduate foundational units in Spiritual Direction, 24 points in Biblical Studies, 24 points in Systematic Theology or Church History, 96 points of postgraduate elective units in Spiritual Direction, Spirituality or Pastoral Theology and Ministry Studies, and either a capstone unit in Spiritual Direction of at least 24 points or RQ9748M Minor Thesis (48 points), with any remaining points made up of further postgraduate units in Spiritual Direction or Spirituality. Standard full-time duration is 2 years (up to 6 years part-time).
c9210db7-77a8-486e-bc52-e4428a6daa8d.admission_requirements: Admission requires successful completion of an undergraduate degree or an approved equivalent. Up to 144 points of credit may be granted, per the University's Credit Policy.
c9210db7-77a8-486e-bc52-e4428a6daa8d.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

f01a2931-0a07-4a07-a936-6c290405338b.name: Master of Theological Studies
f01a2931-0a07-4a07-a936-6c290405338b.description: The Master of Theological Studies enables students to apply an advanced body of knowledge in theology and its associated disciplines, broadening and deepening their engagement with select areas of study to prepare for professional practice and further learning. It is one of the most widely delivered postgraduate awards in the consortium, offered by all 12 University of Divinity member colleges.
f01a2931-0a07-4a07-a936-6c290405338b.curriculum: The award consists of 288 points (12 standard postgraduate units): 72 points of postgraduate foundational units from at least three Fields, 120 points of postgraduate elective units in more than one Field, and either a capstone unit of at least 24 points or RQ9748M Minor Thesis (48 points), with any remaining points made up of further postgraduate units in any discipline. Standard full-time duration is 2 years (up to 6 years part-time). Graduates who complete a Minor Thesis to a specified standard may be eligible for admission to higher degrees by research.
f01a2931-0a07-4a07-a936-6c290405338b.admission_requirements: Admission requires successful completion of an undergraduate degree. Up to 144 points of credit may be granted, including 48 points for the Certificate of Religious Education of the Catholic Diocese of Sale, per the University's Credit Policy.
f01a2931-0a07-4a07-a936-6c290405338b.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy. Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.

65622bd6-8377-4621-be17-c626c8676c41.name: Master of Theology
65622bd6-8377-4621-be17-c626c8676c41.description: The Master of Theology enables students who already hold an undergraduate degree in theology or ministry to apply an advanced body of knowledge in theology and its associated disciplines, deepening engagement with select areas of study for professional practice and further learning. It is delivered by 11 University of Divinity member colleges. Unlike the Master of Philosophy, this is a coursework Master's (not a Higher Degree by Research), even though it includes an optional minor thesis pathway.
65622bd6-8377-4621-be17-c626c8676c41.curriculum: The award consists of 240 points (10 standard postgraduate units): up to 48 points of postgraduate foundational units in any discipline, either a capstone unit of at least 24 points or RQ9748M Minor Thesis (48 points), and further postgraduate elective units in any discipline making up the balance. Standard full-time duration is 2 years (minimum 3 semesters, up to 5 years part-time). Graduates who complete a Minor Thesis to a specified standard may be eligible for admission to higher degrees by research.
65622bd6-8377-4621-be17-c626c8676c41.admission_requirements: Minimum academic requirement is one of a Bachelor of Theology, Bachelor of Ministry, Master of Divinity, or current enrolment in the Bachelor of Theology or Bachelor of Ministry at University of Divinity with at least 378 points completed (to be finished within 12 months of admission). A Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma alone is explicitly insufficient for admission. Probationary admission is not available. Up to 120 points of credit may be granted, per the University's Credit Policy.
65622bd6-8377-4621-be17-c626c8676c41.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 with minimums of 21 Writing/12 Listening/13 Reading/18 Speaking, PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill below 50, or C1 Advanced 169 in each component), per Schedule A (Coursework Awards, AQF 5 to 9) of the University of Divinity Admissions Policy, since the Master of Theology is a coursework award (not classified as Higher Degree by Research on its own live page or in the Higher Degree by Research Policy's Table 1 of HDR entry points). Applicants may also meet the requirement via prior English-medium tertiary study as set out in the same policy.
